The hearings in the matter were held on 20.12.2023, 27.2.2024, 16.7.2024, 9.92024, 23.10.2024 and 8.11.2024, and the order was reserved. 7. This order is passed considering the submissions made by the Petitioner in the Petition vide affidavit dated 25.8.2023 and subsequent affidavits dated 24.11.2023, 18.3.2024, 6.8.2024, and 6.11.2024, reply filed by NRSS vide affidavits dated 8. Having heard the learned counsels of the Petitioner and NRSS, and perused the material on record, we proceed to dispose of the Petition. (f) Regarding the NRSS’s claim that the Petitioner intimated NRSS for the first time qua charging of the transmission asset on 30.6.2022, and the Petitioner ought to have been ready for charging the transmission asset by the next month, i.e., 31.7.2022, there is no incident reported by NRSS wherein any prejudice has been caused to them in the absence of the prior intimation. It has been held by the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (the APTEL) judgment in Fatehgarh Bhadla Transmission Company Limited v. Central Electricity Regulatory Commission & 38. In response, the Petitioner has submitted that in the instant case, the Petitioner has given detailed reasoning regarding the delay caused on account of the commissioning of the associated TBCB Line, the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 and 2021, and the strike by local labourers and villagers. Accordingly, the Petitioner has sought liberty to rely upon the same. - (b) The Petitioner has provided the Form-12 in its TV reply dated 24.11.2023 wherein the Petitioner has given detailed reasons regarding the delay caused on account of the commissioning of the associated TBCB line, the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 and 2021, and the strike by the local labourers and villagers. we are not inclined to consider that at the initial stage, the Petitioner has carried out _ordered lock-down in their State/UTs as per their own assessments. The Petitioner has sought reimbursement of the fees it paid for filing the Petition and for publication expenses. The Petitioner shall be entitled to reimbursement of the filing fees and publication expenses in connection with the present Petition, directly from the beneficiaries on a pro-rata basis in accordance with Regulation 70(1) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations. Petition for allowing it to file a separate Petition for claiming the overall security expenses and consequential IWC has become infructuous. (v)The transmission asset in the instant Petition should be treated independently by the Commission and not in relation to any other proceedings. Further, the subject matter of Petition No. 266/MP/2022 is different from the subject matter in the instant petition. The extension of SCOD as allowed by the Commission is independent of the Petitioner’s claims, and the same should be relied upon by NRSS qua the LTTCs and not the Petitioner. The Petitioner has further submitted that it is also relevant to note that the Commission in the _Force Majeure_ extension Petition, i.e., vide its order dated 14.11.2022 for Petition No. 266/MP/2022, had directed NRSS to approach the Commission seeking _Force Majeure_ relief after the completion of the project. Further, the Petitioner has submitted that the abovementioned Petition and the result of the same are independent and ought not to ## **(c) Regarding the NRSS’s claim that there was no privity of contract between the Petitioner and NRSS** _“14. It is observed that the events cited above are still continuing and the Petitioner has approached the commission for declaration of these events as force majeure events and requested for extension of SCOD of the project in advance. Only Element -1 has been completed. Therefore, we are of the view that since the project has not been completed by the Petitioner till date and is still under implementation, it would not be appropriate to take a view at this stage on the claimed force majeure, Change in Law issues and extension of SCOD. Accordingly, the Petitioner is granted liberty to approach the commission to seek the appropriate relief for force majeure events, after completion of the project”._ 124. This order disposes of Petition No. 327/TT/2023 in terms of the above findings and discussions.
